   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Dave Marriott, NOTTINGHAM



Dear Ron/Bob,

Here are a couple more SAM ROM
bugs...


(i) "EXIT IF" is only allowed if
the LOOP it's exiting from is
unconditional; "LOOP" and "LOOP
IF" use different tokens, and
evidently it only checks for one
of them;


much more annoyingly...

(ii) There STILL seems to be a
bug with large BASIC programs -
I've one which won't CLEAR (or
RUN,which includes CLEAR)but can
load and auto-run from a small
loader program which does the
OPEN TO/CLEAR itself. MERGEing
the program also hangs up (even
allowing for the time a MERGE
normally takes on Sam) but seems
to have worked when you disturb
it by poking the NMI button.Also
direct Basic commands take 6 - 7
seconds to begin yet the program
itself runs efficiently enough
and direct calls to procedures
work instantaneously. I'd be
grateful if you have any info on
this problem, as it makes devel-
opment a right pain.
                 - Dave Marriott

>Dave Marriott from Brian Cavers

I sympathise because I'm also
suffering similar problems while
trying to develop programs. One
in particular is the CONTENTS
BASIC which just fills up to
around 32768(where the next page
boundary begins). While editing,
this sometimes locks up the SAM
or won't run properly.

One thing that often works is to
add a line at the start to move
the end of BASIC well into the
next page (but it certainly does
not always work)...

10 DIM BUG$(5000)      or...

10 REM XXXXXXX (hundreds of x's)

You don't say just how large the
program is. You mention OPEN TO.
A VERY large program obviously
cannot even load unless OPEN TO
is used first [in the same way
that,(as on a Spectrum) if CLEAR
is too low]. If your program is
CLOSE to filling the available
space on the default CLEAR TO it
may not quite have enough room
to initialize variables etc.I've
just realized this means that
ALL large BASIC programs (over
about 60K)must have a pre-loader
to OPEN BASIC!

You might care to send me a copy
of your program to see if I can
find out more as I'm interested
in pinning down some of these
serious bugs.

I'm also compiling a disc of
such faulty programs which I had
intended to pass to Andy Wright
(the SAM BASIC author) at some
time. However, I now doubt that
any further work is being done
or is planned to be done on the
faulty BASIC either because of
SAMCO's lack of funds or lack of
interest. I, for one, would be
greatly encouraged to hear they
are pulling out all the stops
and giving top priority to solve
ALL the faults in the SAM - even
if it takes another year for a
new ROM to be issued.

If you do send your program, let
me know if you want me to stick
it on my bugs compilation disc
as well as see if I can cure it.

Regarding the long delay before
direct commands operate when a
big program is loaded, here are
my thoughts...

We know when a program is run
the SAM first sets up a table of
addresses of GO SUBs, PROCEDUREs
etc. so, once running, no time
is wasted calling a subroutine
(Can anyone tell me where I read
this as I can't find it now!).
This is a great idea although
the table does take some seconds
to first initialize and, I think
we'd all agree, if we had to
choose between a slow-running
program and one that runs
quickly but takes a few seconds
to start we would choose the
latter. However...

I've not written any giant BASIC
programs on the SAM yet but
since getting your letter I put
together a dummy program of 56K.
This takes 20 SECONDS before it
starts to run! However, it does
contain a large number of GOSUBs
so I made a 300K program using
GO TOs. This only took 5 seconds
or so to get going.I've now done
a 200K program using procedures.
This takes 45 seconds! It seems
likely that, despite the large
memory and ability of the SAM to
run large programs in theory, it
may be impractical in fact.

It appears that every time a
line of BASIC is EDITed (even if
no change is made) a flag is set
to say the table is "uncreated".

If you then just enter a direct
command like PRINT 99 it takes
(in my last example) 45 SECONDS
to print it on the screen!
However, once printed, further
direct commands are virtually
instantaneous indicating the SAM
checks that the table is created
every time one enters any
command. It really ought to only
do this if one enters GOTO 5000
or RUN 9900 which effectively
gets the program running. There
may be a reason why it needs to
make sure the table exists while
ALL commands are being processed
but it should have been avoided
if possible.

Here then, are two pointers that
may alleviate the problem...

When developing a program,do not
use RUN but GO TO 1. This won't
make any difference if you have
edited a line meanwhile but does
avoid the delay if not whereas
RUN ALWAYS sets up the table (as
does CLEAR).

Avoid editing a line repeatedly
if, for example, trying various
values in a PLOT and DRAW, edit
the line,delete the line number,
alter the value and enter the
line as a direct command until
you have the value you want then
enter it permanently. Ridiculous
yes but may save exasperation on
occasion. Anybody got any other
ideas on this?
               - Brian

From Ettrick Thomson

OUTLET has not yet mentioned
"Specmaker" from SD Software,
another program for "turning SAM
into a Spectrum". I find it
easier to get on with than
Lerm's program, but when I tried
COPY on my Star LC10II printer,
the x-scale differs from the
y-scale by about 30%.

They can be made equal with a
change of some DATA statements
in "ROMMAKER". MERGE it then
EDIT lines 1032 and 1036 thus...

1032: 2nd row (as LISTed in MODE
4):change ..62,2.. to ..62,1..
which changes LD A,2 to LD A,1,
thereby sending each pixel once.

1036: 3rd row: change ..27,51,
22,27,42,1,0,2.. to ..27,51,24,
27,42,5,0,1.. making the line
spacing 24/216" and selecting
Graphics Mode 5 (72 dots per in)

Some older printers do not have
Mode 5, but have Mode 4 (80 dots
per inch):..27,51,22,27,42,4,0,1
...gives passable results.

You can now RUN this ROMMAKER in
the specified way, loading the
Spectrum ROM from tape but if
you have already created
specrom1 to specrom5, then, by
changing line 60 to LOAD
"specrom1"CODE, and RUNning, you
avoid the tape-loading.

Many thanks Ettrick. - Brian

From John Russell, LONDON, S.W.9

What can I say? Brill, Fab, WOW:
Words fail me. Of course I'm
talking about my first issue of
OUTLET. It's just what I've been
looking for. No more will I
waste pounds on glossy rubbish!
Oh well, that's enough praise -
now my money's worth!

1:What printer do I use with my
  +3?

2:What modem works with my +3?

3:What's the best wordprocessor?

     Thanks, John Russell

P.S.I must recommend P.C.Weekly!

To John Russell from Brian Gaff

Well, we know Brother printers
work well with the +3, but most
recent printers seem OK. Due to
a bug in the +3 ROM, some
printers do not work correctly.
The ones we have heard about are
Citizen 120D, some early STAR
LC10s, and those made by Tandy.

Modem-wise, the Speccy is not
well-served. As far as we know,
nobody produces a modem
interface now. The normal modem
is the VTX 5000, but this has to
be modified to run on the +3. As
mentioned previously, I can
supply these for `20.[See last
month's ADD-VERTS or address on
Page 46 of these OUTLETTERS]

If you are wondering why you
can't just plug one into the +3
RS232, the reason is that it is
driven by software via the sound
chip and cannot operate reliably
in full duplex.

The best word processor really
depends on whether you use CP/M
or not. If you do, then there is
a good one available as PD,
called VDE. If you want one
specifically for the +3, then I
can recommend Tasword +3 and
Tas-spell. Not cheap of course,
but you should find it has every
feature you could want.

                   - Brian Gaff

From: S.J. Nutting, Cambridge.

You might be interested to know
there is a way to speed up copy-
ing discs on Sam DOS 2. First,
you need to find out the last
track the programs use on the
disc you need to copy then POKE
493764,62, track+1,201: Format
"d1:"TO"d2:". The disc will now
format track 0 to the last track
you poked in and copy them. For
example, to copy SC-ASSEMBLER
256 it took 33 secs and 48 secs
for 512. Also if you POKE from
498530 to 498538 with 0 you
cancel the "Are you Sure? y/n".

                S.J. Nutting

Many thanks, Steve.     - Brian

From Malcolm Perry

Regarding FINDOUT (Issue 38),the
routine has been used virtually
unchanged since sending in that
version. There have been a few
minor cosmetic alterations but
rereading the info I spotted a
small error that might confuse.
This relates to non-consecutive
issues. In the example lines,
2100 should read ....

IF A=12 THEN LET A=14

In line 2600 the 13 should be
14.

I should point out that with
this example CC would be set to
=14 and EE =16 in line 2000.

The idea is that the program is
"fooled" to think it has 3
consecutive issues. (14,15 & 16)
instead of 12,15 & 17. Values in
EE & CC are compared with A as
an input error check.


Cosmetic changes:I have realised
since sending the program that
line 9900 of CONTENTS is not
ideal for the added BASIC to set
the ISSUE No. (I$ DATA) on the
disc as every time the Contents
is returned to, it rewrites this
in info to disc which is
unnecessary. It only needs to be
set once on entering a paticular
issue and this is better done in
the AUTOLOAD routine...

CLEAR and MERGE "AUTOLOAD". EDIT
line 50 (normally),by adding the
extra BASIC (as for 9900) in the
line between the CODE"LOAD R"and
the :LOAD d* "CONTENTS" towards
the end of the line.(as an
example from Issue 38). This way
you have the title screen to
look at while the DATA I$ is
being set on the disc.


Finally, when the FINDOUT menu
is on screen it is advantageous
sometimes to know the current
running version of OUTLET. Move
the whole of line 2500 in
FINDOUT to 2010. delete 2500
entirely. In line 2020 add just
after the first PRINT statement
"CURRENT ISSUE ";I$''

Hope this has been of interest.
When it was first written, discs
were about `1.50 (well those I
bought were) and so saved me
about `48 in cost of discs. Good
job discs are a lot cheaper now
OUTLET is a lot bigger! No I'm
certainly not going to complain
about bigger OUTLETS. Anyway,
discs now at 50p (or less) work
out about the same per issue.

Any chance of one or two Christ-
mas screens without the usual
OUTLET info etc. associated with
the title page? - Malcolm Perry

Thanks Malcolm. I had nothing
suitable in stock but made up
"XMASCLIP" which I've coloured
for you! Hope that's suitable.
                        - Brian

From R. Oldroyd, COTTINGHAM

I have just read David Wornham's
letter (Outlet 38 SAM),regarding
producing harmonics (secondary
notes)for a single channel tune.
Even a professional organist,
such as myself,can't add second-
ary notes to a single channel
tune, unless I have some idea of
what chord is supposed to be
played to back that melody.

On a portable keyboard,harmonics
can be added automatically
because a single finger on the
left hand tells the machine the
chord, and the harmonics given
in the chord are used to
compliment the single finger of
the right hand. i.e.,it has more
information available.

Mr. Wornham probably is thinking
of simply adding a second note
of the chord named after the
note played in the single
channel tune. If he goes into
Dixon's and sets a keyboard to
single finger chord, and then
plays his tune in the chord
section, he will find that the
result of harmonics added in
this way is totally non-musical.
I don't believe it can be done.

        Yours faithfully,

              R. Oldroyd




Many thanks for the info.- Brian

From:A.A. Blythe, KIRBY MOORSIDE

Dear Outletters, I was going to
say I'm lost for words - But -

        Yours sincerely,

From: Bryson Hall, W. YORKS.

I know Tasword files are prefer-
able to hand-written letters but
my keyboard membrane is cracking
up (literally). Can anyone tell
me of a supplier who can send me
a membrane I can fit myself.I've
seen several adverts for key -
board repairs but I can't find
anyone to just supply parts.

Now the SAM Coupe; has anyone
managed to connect SAM to an
RGB-TTL monitor? MGT said you
could, warning that RGB monitors
can be either linear or TTL and
that TTL monitors are limited to
16 colours. Anyone know where I
can get a lead? I assume it has
to have a SCART plug at one end

and a TTL RGB DIN 8 pin plug at
the other. Local shops were
incredulous or not interested.
Somebody out there must know.
Please help.

Perhaps someone could write a
feature for Outlet about lead -
pin connections and expanding
the system. The User's Guide,
admirable in many respects,
merely tantalises with a neat
diagram of possibilities on page
108 but no practical basic
information for people with no
specialist knowledge (like me!).

By the way of a "carrot" I am
offering  any one of the
following original software
titles to the first person who


can answer my queries about
membranes and monitors. Chose
any one of these:-

  POWERPRINT:-Buttercraft
              software

  OMNICALC 2:-Microsphere

  PAINTBOX:-

  ARTIST:-    Softeknics

  SUPERCHESS 3.0:-CP Software

  REVOLUTION:-Vortex

  BAZIL THE GREAT MOUSE

  DETECTIVE:- Gremlins graphics

An idea for a future Outlet
which would interest many, I am
sure, is this:"The Men Behind
Outlet"- Who are Ron and Brian?
We know you're witty,intelligent
organised, have a sense of fair-
play and care about quality,
value for money, and give good
"Old-fashioned" service. We know
you are very knowledgeable about
the SPECTRUM and SAM in
particular and probably about
computers generally.We know that
you recognise and appreciate
elegance in programming. I think
some of your personality comes
across through the creativity
you show in the design and prod-
uction of OUTLET but what about
a short biography or a brief
history of OUTLET?

How did you begin the"magazine"?
What about the early programmes
like UTILITIES A/B, PRO-MAT,
BONABANNER, REMSTORE and all
those others? The editorial for
the recent "Birthday" issue
would have been a good time to
answer some of these questions
but it's not too late!

How about digitised pictures of
the famous brothers as an
introductory screen pic. for a
future issue? Just think you
could have people rushing up to
you in the street, pub, doctor's
waiting room asking for
autographs!!
             Yours sincerely,

               Bryson Hall

P.S.

I can't remember exactly what I
said in my last letter about my
SAM and Disciple but I obviously
misled you (unintentionally)
because although they share the
same (Viglen) 5.25" drive, I
have to disconnect - reconnect.
Like you,I would be keen to hear
of ways to cross-connect them!.

To Bryson Hall from Brian Gaff

There are quite a few sources of
membranes, the cost does vary
though. You must specify if you
want an old rubber-keyed Speccy
version, or the one for the
Spectrum+ and 128K machines. I
got all my membranes from P.V.
Tubes on 0254 236521.

The problem with monitors is
that everone has their own idea
of what socket to use.Even those
which use SCART sockets have
different interpretations of the
'standard' which is not helpful.
Quite often leads need to be
tailor-made with resistors fitt-
ed to adjust for gain differ-
ences between different models.

Probably the best people to ask
are PBT Electronics, on 0639
885008. Without knowing what
monitor you have,that's the best
I can do.


I would also ask PBT about the
headphone adaptor, but I think
the level at that socket may be
a bit low to drive them directly
anyway. You really need a small
stereo amplifier to get any
decent sound from SAM.


It will need quite a bit of
research to find out what all
the possibilities for SAM inter-
facing are, even the technical
manual cops out in places!

Well, switching disc drives has
been done, but I have never seen
a commercial product which
claims to do it. Looking at the
number of lines required, it
looks like a Centronics printer
switch might manage it. However,
I would not like to try it with
the equipment on, and turning it
off would slightly defeat the
object! In many cases, the disc
cable must be kept short or it
stops things working correctly.

                 Brian Gaff

[I did start a biography some
time ago but shelved it through
lack of time (sigh! - THAT'S the
story of my life). I will have
another go one day. - B.C.]

From: S. Glenn, Coventry.

Dear Ron and Brian,

I have recently upgraded to a
+D interface and Disc Drive and
would recommend it to anyone
seriously thinking about doing
so.

However, I have encountered a
slight problem while transfering
back issues to Disc.  When
running OUT-TAKE 3: WORD SHOWER
(Issue 5): and L-PROMPT (Issue
5),both programs begin to start
printing to the screen and then
freeze, although you still have
control over the program.

I understand both programs poke
the unused system variable,so if
the +D uses this for its own use
could this be the problem?

Due to a bad connection on the
expansion bus, (my fault), the
computer crashed when the +D
interface was touched.  Although
no damage seems to have been
done and disc operations perform
normally,could this be an under-
lying fault with the +D? As I've
only had it a short while I do
not know how to test every disc
read and write operation.I would
be grateful for any help.

As regards the magazine, keep up
the good work, and how about a
few +D progs/articles? - S.GLENN

To S. Glenn from Brian Gaff.
Some of the very early OUTLET
programs were devised for Micro-
drive and the hanging effect you
describe is due to an incompata-
bility.The large printing relies
on a quirk in the ZX ROM, and I
guess the +D modifies this.After
all, it redirects the Printer
output to its own interface.

Most add-ons suffer from bad
connections at one time or an-
other. The +D is normally reli-
able but if you do have problems
it is quite easy to write a
simple disc verifier in Basic
using LOAD @ in a loop. It is
always a good idea to keep a
back-up of important files as it
only needs a momentary break in
power to corrupt a disc! - B.G.

From C.E.B. Powell.
When wishing to explore OUTLET
programs on my +3, I often use
the SPECTRUM command, as this
pages in the normal character
set. Since a writer in Issue 37
came up with the idea of calling
the paging routine at 23354, I
have been able to re-enter 128K
Basic without merging in any
other 48-128 mini-programs. This
works but can result in the
drive motor not being switched
off when a disk is next accessed
- have you any ideas on how to
avoid this? When combinations of
keys were pressed together, such
as the 'HELLO I'M A +3' led me
to experiment and I have found
the following BASIC editing
commands which don't appear to
be mentioned in the manual...

SYMBOLSHIFT 'I' drops the cursor
down through a program in steps
of approximately 10 lines.  In
GRAPHICS mode; 'V' moves the
cursor to the end of the program
and 'W' back to the beginning.
'X' moves the cursor to the end
of the current line, and 'Y'
takes it back to the start. 'Z'
toggles between the full screen
and lower screen Editing modes
without going through the Edit
menu.GRAPH needs to be hit again
before editing a line. Someone
spent the time and trouble to
write the code supporting these
commands so why on earth are
they not documented?! A
disassembly of the +3's multi
ROMs is long overdue.

Finally, can you suggest an
inexpensive modem to allow me
access to Prestel? The +3 seems
oblivious to its connection to
to my VTX 5000. Many thanks for
a great magazine.

              C.E.B. Powell

To C.E.B.Powell from Brian Gaff

Regarding the +3 mode switching,
if I POKE 23611 with 221 after
returning to 128K mode, I find
the disk normally stops.However,
if you really want an instant
stop during a program, try POKE
23388,4.

The +3's extended editing
commands are left over from the
original black 128K Spectrum.
The idea was that a small add-on
keypad would be produced that
would plug into the Aux port.
This would then give access to
these commands. Unfortunately,
Amstrad decided not to bother
with this, and removed the Aux
port software. This left the


rather obscure key presses as
the only way to get at the edit-
ing commands! I agree, it is a
shame but that's (Amstrad) life!

I doubt if there's enough inter-
est in the Spectrum now for any-
one to want to do a disassembly
of the newer ROMs. I have seen a
neat program that can save all
four out to disc though, if you
fancy the job!

Ah, the dreaded +3 expansion
port botch up strikes again! I
can help here, as on Micronet,
we had to find a way of getting
the VTX5000 going on the +3. I
now have a small stock of some-
thing we call The FIXIT, that
unscrambles Amstrad's handywork.

It just plugs into the Spectrum
+3 or +2A, and the VTX's ribbon
cable just plugs into that. If
you, or anyone else for that
matter, are interested, I can
supply them at `9:50.

Available from me at 64 Roebuck
Road, Chessington, Surrey KT9
1JX(Cheques and POs made payable
to B.G. Services).

                     Brian G..

Dear Ron/Bob,

Here are a couple more SAM ROM bugs...

(i) "EXIT IF" is only allowed if the LOOP it's exiting from is unconditional; "LOOP" and "LOOP IF" use different tokens, and evidently it only checks for one of them;

I sympathise because I'm also suffering similar problems while trying to develop programs. One in particular is the CONTENTS BASIC which just fills up to around 32768(where the next page boundary begins). While editing, this sometimes locks up the SAM or won't run properly.

One thing that often works is to add a line at the start to move the end of BASIC well into the next page (but it certainly does not always work)...

10 DIM BUG$(5000)      or...

10 REM XXXXXXX (hundreds of x's)

You don't say just how large the program is. You mention OPEN TO. A VERY large program obviously cannot even load unless OPEN TO is used first [in the same way that,(as on a Spectrum) if CLEAR is too low]. If your program is CLOSE to filling the available space on the default CLEAR TO it may not quite have enough room to initialize variables etc.I've just realized this means that ALL large BASIC programs (over about 60K)must have a pre-loader to OPEN BASIC!

You might care to send me a copy of your program to see if I can find out more as I'm interested in pinning down some of these serious bugs.

I'm also compiling a disc of such faulty programs which I had intended to pass to Andy Wright (the SAM BASIC author) at some time. However, I now doubt that any further work is being done or is planned to be done on the faulty BASIC either because of SAMCO's lack of funds or lack of interest. I, for one, would be greatly encouraged to hear they are pulling out all the stops and giving top priority to solve ALL the faults in the SAM - even if it takes another year for a new ROM to be issued.

If you do send your program, let me know if you want me to stick it on my bugs compilation disc as well as see if I can cure it.

Regarding the long delay before direct commands operate when a big program is loaded, here are my thoughts...

We know when a program is run the SAM first sets up a table of addresses of GO SUBs, PROCEDUREs etc. so, once running, no time is wasted calling a subroutine (Can anyone tell me where I read this as I can't find it now!). This is a great idea although the table does take some seconds to first initialize and, I think we'd all agree, if we had to choose between a slow-running program and one that runs quickly but takes a few seconds to start we would choose the latter. However...

I've not written any giant BASIC programs on the SAM yet but since getting your letter I put together a dummy program of 56K. This takes 20 SECONDS before it starts to run! However, it does contain a large number of GOSUBs so I made a 300K program using GO TOs. This only took 5 seconds or so to get going.I've now done a 200K program using procedures. This takes 45 seconds! It seems likely that, despite the large memory and ability of the SAM to run large programs in theory, it may be impractical in fact.

It appears that every time a line of BASIC is EDITed (even if no change is made) a flag is set to say the table is "uncreated".

If you then just enter a direct command like PRINT 99 it takes (in my last example) 45 SECONDS to print it on the screen! However, once printed, further direct commands are virtually instantaneous indicating the SAM checks that the table is created every time one enters any command. It really ought to only do this if one enters GOTO 5000 or RUN 9900 which effectively gets the program running. There may be a reason why it needs to make sure the table exists while ALL commands are being processed but it should have been avoided if possible.

Here then, are two pointers that may alleviate the problem...

When developing a program,do not use RUN but GO TO 1. This won't make any difference if you have edited a line meanwhile but does avoid the delay if not whereas RUN ALWAYS sets up the table (as does CLEAR).

Avoid editing a line repeatedly if, for example, trying various values in a PLOT and DRAW, edit the line,delete the line number, alter the value and enter the line as a direct command until you have the value you want then enter it permanently. Ridiculous yes but may save exasperation on occasion. Anybody got any other ideas on this? - Brian

Возможно, вам будет интересно узнать, что существует способ ускорить копирование дисков в Sam DOS 2. Сначала вам нужно узнать последнюю дорожку, которую программы занимают на диске, который вы хотите скопировать, а затем ввести:

```text
POKE 493764,62, track+1,201: Format "d1:"TO"d2:"
```

Теперь диск отформатирует дорожки от 0 до последней указанной вами дорожки и скопирует их. Например, копирование SC-ASSEMBLER 256 заняло 33 секунды, а для версии 512 — 48 секунд. Кроме того, если сделать POKE с 498530 по 498538 нулями, вы отключите запрос "Are you Sure? y/n".

В строках примера строка 2100 должна выглядеть так:

```text
IF A=12 THEN LET A=14
```

В строке 2600 число 13 должно быть заменено на 14.

Следует отметить, что в этом примере CC будет установлено в =14, а EE =16 в строке 2000.

Идея состоит в том, чтобы «обмануть» программу, заставив её думать, что у неё 3 последовательных выпуска (14, 15 и 16) вместо 12, 15 и 17. Значения в EE и CC сравниваются с A для проверки ошибок ввода.

SYMBOL SHIFT 'I' перемещает курсор вниз по программе с шагом примерно в 10 строк. В режиме GRAPHICS: 'V' перемещает курсор в конец программы, а 'W' — обратно в начало.
